title: Onboard Eval Signal Heap: regression triage and action plan
body:
Purpose
------
This is a working synthesis of onboarding evaluation signals for the last 14 days (2026-03-05 -> 2026-03-18). Goal: condense the noisy alerts from the automated evals and promptset runs into a small set of prioritized failures we can act on before the next on-call rotation. This is not the final postmortem — think of it as the signal heap: sorted, annotated, and action-ready.

Top-level summary (TL;DR)
-----------------------
- Overall regression rate increased from 3.1% -> 6.8% across the primary onboarding promptsets. Biggest spike occurred around 2026-03-11 after model variant roll (v1.8.Q -> v1.9.Q-lite).
- Failure modes cluster into three families: hallucinated factual claims (35% of failures), truncated completions (25%), and formatting/JSON-structure mismatches (18%).
- Promptset coverage gap: 22% of incoming onboarding prompts (by traffic tail) are not covered by canonical eval promptsets; those uncovered examples explain ~40% of high-severity failures.
- Immediate action items (high priority): roll back the v1.9.Q-lite rollout for dedicated infra experiments; backfill promptset coverage for top-10 uncovered intents; add a targeted unit eval for KV-cache edge cases.

Metrics snapshot (automated dashboards)
-------------------------------------
- Weekly regression signal trend (alerts/day): 2026-03-05: 12, 03-09: 18, 03-11: 46, 03-14: 31, 03-18: 20.
- Severity breakdown (last 14d): Sev1 (user-impacting incorrect facts) = 14, Sev2 (partial/formatting) = 42, Sev3 (style/regression non-blocking) = 67.
- Promptset coverage: canonical set covers 78% of incoming intents; uncovered tail has heavy long-tail prompts from two enterprise customers.
- Median latency during regressions: +12% over baseline; p95 unchanged.

Top failure clusters (ranked)
---------------------------
1) Hallucinated Citations / Bad-Reference (35% of failures)
   - Symptom: model confidently fabricates source titles or dates when asked for references.
   - Trigger: longer context (>1200 tokens) + recently introduced attention kernel change in v1.9.Q-lite.
   - Representative example: "Cites: Journal of Distributed Systems, 2025" when no such article exists.
   - Hypotheses: kernel selection interacts poorly with citation prompt templates that rely on truncated context; KV cache eviction timing causes stale prefixes to influence generations.

2) Truncation and token drop at sequence boundary (25%)
   - Symptom: generation cuts off mid-sentence when context has many short quotes + list tokens.
   - Trigger: batching heuristic + sequence-length estimation mismatch on dedicated infra.
   - Note: p95 latency stable, but throughput optimizations (aggressive batching) appear correlated.

3) JSON / structured-output formatting regressions (18%)
   - Symptom: invalid JSON (missing commas, extra brackets) from structured-output prompts.
   - Trigger: promptset variants that rely on soft constraints; regression surfaced after tokenizer change in v1.9-lite.

4) Small-class semantic swaps (12%)
   - Symptom: synonyms replaced incorrectly in domain-specific promptsets (finance/legal).
   - Trigger: model tokenization/embedding drift after quantization profile tweak.

5) Low-confidence hallucination (10%)
   - Symptom: plausible-sounding but wrong facts (low confidence scores flagged by detectors).

Promptset analysis and coverage notes
------------------------------------
- Top 10 uncovered intents (by incoming traffic contribution) identified — two are enterprise-specific: "policy-explain-v2" and "legacy-invoice-extraction". We should add 50 canonical prompts for these intents to the onboarding suite.
- Several prompt paraphrases (common on customer requests) are missing; add a lightweight paraphrase generator to expand canonical sets automatically, then validate with synthetic adversarial checks.

Triage timeline and quick root-cause mapping
------------------------------------------
- 03-10: v1.9.Q-lite staged to 10% (A/B). No immediate flags.
- 03-11: automated evals spike; first human review flagged hallucinated citations.
- 03-12: deeper sampling shows truncation patterns on sequences >1600 tokens.
- 03-13: developer experiment toggling kernel back to legacy removes hallucination in 30% of cases (local repro).
- 03-16: temp rollback on a customer canary reduced Sev1 events by 60%.

Immediate recommended actions (owners + ETA)
------------------------------------------
- ACTION A (Owner: Ravi) — Emergency rollback of v1.9.Q-lite on dedicated pool used by onboarding runs. ETA: 24 hours. Priority: P0.
- ACTION B (Owner: Anika) — Expand onboarding promptset: add top-10 uncovered intents + 50 paraphrases for each; create automated generator sweep. ETA: 7 days. Priority: P0/P1.
- ACTION C (Owner: Diego) — Add a KV-cache unit test (repro harness) to the runtime testbench and a nightly regression job that targets context lengths 1200-2200 tokens. ETA: 5 days. Priority: P1.
- ACTION D (Owner: Maya) — Add a structured-output strict validator in eval pipeline (JSON lint + schema enforcement) and fail the run if invalid. ETA: 3 days. Priority: P1.
- ACTION E (Owner: SRE eng rotation) — Temporarily reduce aggressive batching heuristic for onboarding evals to baseline settings until we have a fix. ETA: 48 hours. Priority: P1.

Planned experiments (short list)
-------------------------------
- Kernel ablation: compare v1.9.Q-lite kernels with legacy kernel under identical context distributions (owner: runtime team).
- KV-eviction timing sweep: measure hallucination frequency vs KV eviction intervals (owner: Diego).
- Prompt softness calibration: evaluate structured-output prompts with stronger constraint tokens vs soft templates.

Monitoring/alerts changes (quick wins)
------------------------------------
- Add a dedicated "citation-hallucination" detector that looks for fabricated tokens matching pattern ("Journal", dates, DOI patterns).
- Tag onboarding eval alerts with prompt-intent labels so we can slice by enterprise customers quickly.
- Add a rolling-24h delta alert when seed coverage of promptsets drops below 75% of live intents.

Open questions / unresolved items
-------------------------------
- Why did kernel selection switch to the new kernel path for ~10% of requests in the canary? Need runtime telemetry mapping (kernel id -> request id).
- Is the tokenizer change that shipped alongside v1.9.Q-lite fully backward compatible for low-frequency domain tokens?
- Can we prioritize promptset backfill for two enterprise customers with temporary feature flags?

Notes to reviewers
------------------
- This is intentionally compact; please add inline replies with findings or attach small repro snippets.
- If you are the runtime owner on call, confirm rollback timelines in the thread.
- If you own one of the prompt intents listed, mark claim by replying here and create the PR in eval-playbooks.

Appendix: representative examples (anonymized)
---------------------------------------------
1) Factual hallucination: "According to the Journal of Applied AI (2025), ..." -> No such article exists.
2) Truncation: input long-context -> output ends with "..." mid-phrase.
3) JSON fail: expected {"amount": 123, "currency": "USD"} but got {"amount": 123 "currency": "USD"}.

-- end signal heap --

Next check-in: Fri 2026-03-20 10:00am PT (sprint triage).
